issues.description: Attributes numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents: In problem_statement.md the UML declares these two fields as double, but in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java they are declared as int. This mismatch leaves students unsure whether to implement these attributes as double or int and may cause them to choose the wrong type when writing getters, setters and arithmetic using these fields.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute types consistent across artifacts. Preferred fixes: (a) Change the UML in problem_statement.md to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int to match the solution and typical student counts, or (b) change the solution and template to use double for these two attributes and update all related methods (getters, setters, arithmetic) and tests to use double. Document the chosen type in the textual task description so students are not confused.

issues.description: Method return type for getTotalNumberOfStudents(): In problem_statement.md the UML declares the student-count attributes as double but declares getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, creating an internal inconsistency in the specification. In the solution (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) both the attributes and getTotalNumberOfStudents() are implemented as int, so the UML's mixed types (double attributes vs int return) will confuse students about the intended return type for the total.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the UML inconsistency by choosing one consistent numeric type for student counts and totals. Either (a) change the UML attributes to int so getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int is consistent, or (b) change getTotalNumberOfStudents() in the UML to return double and update the template and solution to use double for attributes and the method return type. Also update any descriptive text to state explicitly whether student counts and totals are integers or floating-point values.
